tagline: An Express API that takes orders and charges payments, with a Playwright end-to-end suite and a small Python worker.

start_here.why: boots the app, mounts routes and opens the database connection
the core business flow: charge, then save
how the end-to-end suite exercises it

diagrams.title: How demo-checkout fits together
diagrams.summary: Browsers call the API, which charges an external payment provider and stores orders. CI runs the Playwright suite against it; a Python worker runs background jobs.
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  user["Browser / client"] -->|"POST /orders"| api["Checkout API (Express)"]
  subgraph runtime["Runs in production"]
    api -->|"charge"| pay["Payment provider (external)"]
    api -->|"save"| db[("Database via Prisma")]
    worker["Python worker"] -.->|"reads"| db
  end
  ci["CI: GitHub Actions"] -->|"runs"| e2e["Playwright suite"]
  e2e -->|"drives"| api
diagrams.legend: Dashed line: link inferred from naming, not from visible code.

components.name: Python worker
components.role: Background jobs such as emails and cleanup

diagrams.title: Inside the API
diagrams.summary: Requests flow from routes to services to the db layer. Nothing depends back upward.
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  server["server.ts (boot)"] --> routes["routes/"]
  server --> db["db/"]
  routes --> services["services/"]
  services --> db

diagrams.title: Placing an order
diagrams.summary: One POST /orders request from route to database.
diagrams.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant R as routes
  participant S as services/orders
  participant P as Payment provider
  participant D as db
  C->>R: POST /orders
  R->>S: createOrder
  S->>P: charge
  S->>D: save
  S-->>C: order JSON

where_to_change.notes: Charging is isolated here, so a new provider should only need this file plus config.
Reuse the checkout fixture; add page objects under tests/pages/.

glossary.meaning: A paid purchase created by POST /orders.
A Playwright helper that prepares objects (like a page object) for each test and cleans up afterwards.
The Python process in worker/ that runs background jobs such as sending emails and cleanup.

gotchas: Imports use the @db/* alias defined in tsconfig.json.
The worker is Python while everything else is TypeScript, so changes to shared data shapes need updating in both places.
open_questions: How does the worker get its jobs? Nothing in the repo shows a queue.
